extracted.intended_audience: claimants, respondents, legal counsel, and authorized representatives appearing before the U.S. Copyright Claims Board (CCB)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and standards governing smaller-claims proceedings, default determinations, claimant failures to proceed, record access, reconsideration/Register review, and party conduct before the Copyright Claims Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claimant's choice to use smaller claims procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimant may request consideration of a claim under the smaller claim procedures at the time of filing and may change that choice any time before service of the initial notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If initial notice already issued, claimant must request reissuance indicating updated choice. Once initial notice has been served on any respondent, claimant may not amend its choice without consent of other parties and leave of the Board. (§226.2)

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterclaim monetary cap in smaller claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may assert a counterclaim only if it seeks total monetary relief of $5,000 or less (exclusive of attorneys' fees or costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any permissible counterclaims shall be adjudicated under the smaller claims procedures set forth in this part. (§226.3)

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-Officer adjudication for smaller claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Smaller claims proceedings shall be heard by one Copyright Claims Officer (Officer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the three Officers shall hear smaller claims proceedings on a rotating basis at the Board's discretion. (§226.4(a))

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial scheduling order prerequisites and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Board issues an initial scheduling order once proceeding is active, second filing fee paid, and the 14-day period in §222.7 completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduling order includes dates/deadlines for filing responses and an initial conference with the presiding Officer. The Board or Officer may amend or issue additional scheduling orders at discretion or upon party request under §222.11(d). (§226.4(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial conference replaces pre-discovery conference
rubrics_metrics.description: An initial conference will take the place of the pre-discovery conference in non-smaller claims proceedings and is used to explain steps, discuss claims, defenses, and settlement possibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While presiding Officer may discuss settlement, any separate settlement conference must be before an Officer who is not the presiding Officer. (§226.4(c)(1))

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery is narrowly tailored in smaller claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Any order requiring documents or information must be narrowly tailored to the merits and highly likely to lead to information relevant to core issues without imposing undue burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If presiding Officer determines such documents are necessary, the Officer shall order parties to serve them and set service deadlines. (§226.4(c)(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: Merits conference scheduling and pre-conference submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding Officer schedules a merits conference during or following the initial conference; parties must file evidence no later than 14 days before the merits conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence filed must have been served on other parties before filing (unless received from other side). Parties may submit a written statement of positions and damages (limited to seven pages under §220.5(b)); no written responses permitted. (§226.4(d)(1)-(2)(i)-(ii))

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness statements and appearance requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may submit witness statements complying with §222.15(b)(2). Opposing party may request witness appear at merits conference no later than seven days before conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure of a witness to appear does not preclude acceptance of the statement, but Officer may consider inability to question witness when weighing testimony. (§226.4(d)(2)(iii))

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for failure to submit evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party fails to submit evidence per Officer's request or submits improperly served evidence, the presiding Officer may address the failure during the merits conference or schedule a separate conference and determine an appropriate remedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies include but are not limited to drawing an adverse inference with respect to disputed facts pursuant to 17 U.S.C. 1506(n)(3), if in interests of justice. (§226.4(d)(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of merits conference
rubrics_metrics.description: During the merits conference each party has opportunity to address submitted materials and present positions on claims, defenses, counterclaims and damages; Officer may ask questions of parties or witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed findings of fact and party response
rubrics_metrics.description: Following merits conference, presiding Officer prepares proposed findings of fact (including any adverse inference) and serves them on each party; parties have 21 days to submit a written response limited to five pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses must follow §220.5(b) and may not reference or attach evidence not previously filed unless leave granted; if leave granted, other parties get opportunity to respond to new evidence. (§226.4(e)(1))

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages election timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimant or counterclaimant seeking damages must state whether seeking statutory damages or actual damages and any profits, if not already elected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This election may be changed at any time up until a final determination. The statement may be included in response to proposed findings of fact. (§226.4(e)(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary agreement to stop/mitigate unlawful activity considered only for damages
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may inform the presiding Officer that if found liable it would voluntarily agree to an order to cease or mitigate the unlawful activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such information shall not be considered for liability but may be considered in determining damages. Election may be made up to and including the merits conference. (§226.4(e)(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Final determination issuance and default transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: After considering information and arguments, the presiding Officer shall issue a final determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If respondent fails to appear/participate as described in §227.1, the presiding Officer shall transfer proceedings to the default rules (part 227), which may result in a default determination or dismissal. A default determination must be issued by no fewer than two Officers. If respondent cures missed deadline, proceeding resumes under these procedures and scheduling order revised if necessary. (§226.4(f))

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional conferences discretionary
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding Officer may hold additional conferences to manage proceedings, address disputes, or discuss settlement upon request or its own initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests and responses for conferences follow procedures in §220.5(a)(1). (§226.4(g))

rubrics_metrics.name: No expert testimony in smaller claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may not submit expert testimony for consideration in smaller claims proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any expert testimony submitted shall be disregarded by the assigned Officer. (§226.4(h))

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of missed deadline for respondent (default notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: If respondent fails to file a response or meet a deadline without justifiable cause, the Board may issue a notice informing respondent that failure may result in a default determination and explain legal effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice provides 30 days from date to cure the missed deadline or requirement and is issued via eCCB, mail, and all known email addresses. (§227.1(a)-(b)(1))

rubrics_metrics.name: Second default notice procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If respondent fails to respond within 15 days after first notice of pending default, Board shall send a second notice attaching the first and reminding respondent of 30-day cure period measured from date of first notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's possible responses to default notice
rubrics_metrics.description: If respondent cures, proceeding resumes; if fails to cure but indicates intent to re-engage, Board may grant additional time or proceed with default determination process; if no response, Board requires claimant to submit evidence to support default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to issue notices and responses follow §220.5(a)(1). (§227.1(c))

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple missed-deadline rule for respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may cure missed deadlines at least twice without default being issued; if respondent misses a third deadline without good cause the Board may proceed directly to requiring submission of evidence for a default determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required from claimant for default determination
rubrics_metrics.description: If respondent ceases to participate and Board proceeds to a default determination, claimant must submit written direct testimony as set forth in §222.15(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submission, Board may request any additional evidence within claimant's possession. (§227.2(a)-(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Board consideration for proposed default determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Board reviews claimant's submitted evidence to determine if it's sufficient under applicable law and considers whether respondent has a meritorious defense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sufficient, Board prepares proposed default determination including relief and damages; if insufficient, Board prepares proposed determination dismissing proceeding without prejudice and allows claimant up to 30 days (7 pages) to respond. (§227.3(a))

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of proposed default determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed default determination shall include a finding in favor of claimant and the damages awarded, if any, and shall include dismissal of any counterclaims asserted by the defaulting respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to respondent of proposed default determination and response period
rubrics_metrics.description: Board shall provide written notice to respondent of the proposed default determination, explain its legal significance, attach the proposed determination, and give respondent 30 days to submit any evidence or information in opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice period begins on the date of the notice. (§227.3(c))

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and timing of respondent's opposition to proposed default
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may submit in writing any evidence or information in opposition within 30 days (absent extension); form must follow written response testimony procedures under §222.15(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If respondent fails to timely submit evidence but indicates intent to submit, Board may grant additional time or proceed. (§227.4(a))

rubrics_metrics.name: Other parties' opportunity to reply to respondent submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If respondent submits evidence in opposition, other parties may address that submission by filing written reply testimony within 21 days of respondent's submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies must follow procedures for written reply testimony under §222.15(c). (§227.4(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Board discretion to hold hearings on default determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Board may hold a hearing related to default determinations at its discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of respondent submitting evidence after proposed default
rubrics_metrics.description: If respondent provides evidence or information in response, Board shall consider all submissions and then maintain or amend its proposed determination; the resulting determination is not a 'default determination' but a final determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a determination may not be challenged under 17 U.S.C. 1508(c)(1)(C) and may only be reconsidered under 17 U.S.C. 1506(w) and procedures in part 230. (§227.5(a))

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed default becomes final if respondent fails to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If respondent fails to respond to notice of pending default, the Board shall issue the proposed default determination as a final determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent may only challenge such determination to the extent permitted under 17 U.S.C. 1508(c) or specified procedures. (§227.5(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Vacating a default determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may request in writing that a default determination be vacated and provide reasons; request must be filed within 30 days, no more than 12 pages, and meet §220.5(b) requirements; response to request due within 30 days and no more than 12 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may vacate the default determination in the interests of justice. (§227.5(c))

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to serve respondents who are unnecessary or necessary parties
rubrics_metrics.description: If claimant fails to timely complete service on a respondent who is not necessary, Board shall dismiss that respondent without prejudice and continue against remaining respondents; if necessary party not served, Board shall dismiss proceeding without prejudice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim requires service on at least one respondent; complete failure to file any proof of service results in dismissal without prejudice. (§228.1(a)-(c))

rubrics_metrics.name: Claimant/counterclaimant failure to prosecute notice and cure
rubrics_metrics.description: If claimant or counterclaimant fails to proceed in an active proceeding (misses deadlines/requirements), Board shall issue a notice informing party that failure may result in dismissal; notice gives 30 days to respond/cure and is sent by mail and email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no response after 15 days, Board sends second notice attaching first. Requests and responses follow §220.5(a)(1). (§228.2(a)-(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Responses and remedies for claimant failure to prosecute
rubrics_metrics.description: If claimant cures in time, proceeding resumes; if fails but signals intent to re-engage, Board may grant more time or issue a determination dismissing claims; if fails to cure and does not respond, Board shall issue a determination dismissing the claims or counterclaims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dismissal determination may include award of attorneys' fees and costs where appropriate. (§228.2(c)-(d))

rubrics_metrics.name: Vacating dismissal for failure to prosecute
rubrics_metrics.description: If no additional proceedings initiated under 17 U.S.C.1508(c), claimant may request vacatur within 30 days, no more than 12 pages and meeting §220.5(b); response within 30 days no more than 12 pages; Board may vacate in interests of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple missed-deadline rule for claimants
rubrics_metrics.description: Claimant or counterclaimant may cure missed deadlines at least twice without dismissal; if a third deadline missed without good cause, Board may proceed directly to dismissal for failure to prosecute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official written record composition and public access
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions by parties and documents issued by the Board constitute the official written record; any member of the public may inspect the official written record through eCCB except materials marked confidential under §222.19.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance restrictions at hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Attendance at Board hearings (including virtual) limited to parties, legal counsel or authorized representatives, and witnesses, except with leave of the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may order a witness excluded from a hearing except when a question is directed to that witness. Requests for third-party non-witness attendance follow §220.5(a)(2). (§229.1(c))

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing transcript procedures and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Board may cause a transcript to be made by official reporter or technology; at a party's request Board may designate an official reporter to attend/transcribe and the requesting party(ies) shall pay the reporter directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to designate official reporter follow §220.5(a)(1). (§229.1(d))

rubrics_metrics.name: Record certification process
rubrics_metrics.description: Official record of a proceeding will be certified upon written request to Records Research and Certification Section and payment of appropriate fee pursuant to 37 CFR 201.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration request timing and content limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request reconsideration of a final determination within 30 days of the determination; request must be no more than 12 pages and meet §220.5(b) requirements and must identify a clear error of law or fact material to the outcome or a technical mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must not merely repeat prior arguments and applies to amended final determinations as well. (§230.1-230.2)

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: A party opposing a request for reconsideration may file a response within 30 days of service; response limited to 12 pages and must meet §220.5(b) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new evidence on reconsideration except under narrow circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence not previously submitted shall not be submitted with a request for reconsideration or response, except where the party demonstrates by clear and convincing evidence that it was not available with reasonable diligence prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decision on reconsideration based on written submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: After response period, Board shall consider the request and any response and either deny or issue an amended final determination, basing decision on written submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register's review limited to abuse-of-discretion after reconsideration denial
rubrics_metrics.description: A party whose request for reconsideration has been denied may seek Register of Copyrights review within 30 days; the Register's review is limited to whether the Board abused its discretion in denying reconsideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be filed within 30 days of denial, no more than 12 pages, meet §220.5(b), be accompanied by the filing fee in 37 CFR 201.3(g)(3), and include reasons why denial was an abuse of discretion. (§231.1-231.5)

rubrics_metrics.name: Register review procedural limits and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposing party may respond within 30 days (12 pages); no new evidence; no reply allowed; Register may deny or remand proceeding to Board for reconsideration and issuance of amended final determination based on written submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants' duty of respectful and truthful conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants (parties, counsel, authorized representatives) shall act with utmost respect for others and behave ethically and truthfully in connection with all submissions and appearances before the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications required for representations to the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: By submitting materials or advocating positions, a participant certifies that, after reasonable inquiry, the submission is not for an improper purpose; legal contentions are made in good faith; factual contentions have evidentiary support or likely will after reasonable investigation; denials have evidentiary support or are reasonably based on belief or lack of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bad-faith conduct sanctions and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Board shall award costs and attorneys' fees as part of a determination where participant engaged in bad-faith conduct, unless inconsistent with interests of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may on its own order a participant to show cause and the accused must file response within 14 days. A party may request a conference describing alleged bad-faith conduct and attach exhibits. After response or lapse of time, Board shall either determine no bad-faith occurred or schedule a conference concerning allegations. (§232.3(a)-(c))

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination and limits on bad-faith awards
rubrics_metrics.description: When awarding attorneys' fees and costs for bad-faith conduct, the Board will consider requests/responses, arguments, and the accused's behavior in other proceedings; award is limited to $5,000 unless adversely affected party was pro se (costs limited to $2,500) or extraordinary circumstances (pattern/practice) justify exceeding limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any award shall be made as part of the final determination. (§232.3(d))

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties and bar for repeated bad-faith conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: A participant found to have engaged in bad-faith conduct on more than one occasion within a 12-month period shall be subject to penalties including potential bar on initiating and participating in claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may on its own order show-cause why conduct engaged in on more than one occasion does not constitute a pattern; party may file request describing instances and include CCB case numbers and exhibits. Such requests filed before opt-out deadlines do not waive opt-out rights. (§232.4(a)-(b))
